source: NSE daily bhavcopy, every session, delisted companies included
universe: NSE stocks trading Rs 10 crore a day or more, priced Rs 20 or more
rules: Bought at the next session's open, held for the period, left on a close under the exit line. Price returns before costs and tax. Index: Nifty 500.
lists_note: month, results and long are the three fundamental lists of December 2026, recipe '2026-12 fundamental lists v3': the site's own engine replayed point in time on prices and filings by research/fundamental_ideas_lab.py, each the version a rule declared before the run chose (see each list's lab). The setup lists are the engine's own replay too (ideas_study.py --setups). This week and momentum, which they replaced, are under retired as last measured.

month.what: Market leaders (leader score in the top 30%) in an uptrend and outside the most volatile fifth, in an industry in the top half on money flow, with no loss and no fall in profit last quarter, no results the market sold in the last month and no more than 10% of the company pledged. Ranked on the month's pullback, closeness to the 52-week high, the last quarter's sales and margin growth, the industry's money flow and a live catalyst; at most four from one industry.
month.bias: Pledges, deliveries and orders have no history to replay: they were unknown here, which the list counts as neutral, and the live list reads them. Industries are NSE's list as it stands today. Quarterly filings start in 2018 and cover companies listed today; a stock with none is never refused for it, and a revised quarter is seen from the revision's date.
month.replay: The site's own engine (backend/leaders.rank) run on every fifth session from 2017, on prices and filings cut at that session; its top fifteen bought at the next open.

lab.rule: Highest first-window mean lead over the average liquid stock, among versions with enough picks and a positive mean after a 0.49% round trip; within 0.05 points the one with fewer rules. The second window is printed whatever it shows.

results.what: Liquid companies whose quarterly results were first priced in the last 10 sessions and showed real growth: sales up 8% or more, profit and operating profit up, other income no more than 35% and an exceptional gain no more than 30% of profit before tax, and cash from operations positive in the last full year. Not already up 18% on the day, nor more than 15% under the 200-day average. Ranked half on that session's move less the average liquid stock's, a quarter on the volume behind it and a quarter on the growth; at most four from one industry. A list is made only when eight or more pass every test.
results.bias: The results tables hold companies listed today, so one delisted after a bad quarter is missing, and a revised quarter is seen from the revision's date with the revised figures. vs_reporters compares the list with every liquid company whose results were priced in the same ten sessions, which shares that bias.
results.replay: The site's own engine (backend/leaders.rank) run on every fifth session from 2017, on prices and filings cut at that session; its top fifteen bought at the next open.

lab.rule: Highest first-window mean lead over the average liquid stock, among versions with enough picks and a positive mean after a 0.49% round trip; within 0.05 points the one with fewer rules. The second window is printed whatever it shows.

long.what: Above the 200-day average and outside the most volatile fifth, a profit over the last four quarters, an F-score of 5 or more, no more than 5% pledged, a return on capital of 14% or more, cash from operations positive and at least 0.7 times profit, debt no more than equity (a lender: a return on equity of 13% or more), and a P/E under 90 unless its PEG is 1.5 or under on profit growing 35% a year. Ranked on quality, three-year compounding, governance, valuation against its own industry and the year-long trend; at most four from one industry.
long.bias: Balance sheets are on file from September 2022 and full-year cash flows from 2020-21. Before then the return, debt, F-score and cash checks were skipped as unknown and the list ranked mostly on its trend, which is why its version was chosen on 2022-11 to 2024-04. Pledges and holdings have no history and were unknown throughout. The tables hold companies listed today, and a revised filing is seen from the revision's date.
long.replay: The site's own engine (backend/leaders.rank) run on every fifth session from 2017, on prices and filings cut at that session; its top fifteen bought at the next open.

lab.rule: Highest first-window mean lead over the average liquid stock, among versions with enough picks and a positive mean after a 0.49% round trip; within 0.05 points the one with fewer rules. The second window is printed whatever it shows.

short.what: A close above a 40-session range 18% wide or tighter on twice the usual volume in the last five sessions, still above it; above the 200-day average; leader score in the top half; six or more of nine chart conditions; its industry in the top half on money flow; no fall in profit last quarter; results, if just out, not sold by the market.
short.replay: The site's own engine run on every fifth session; its top fifteen bought at the next open.
short.bias: Industries are NSE's list as it stands today, and quarterly results start in 2018 and cover companies listed today. Before 2018 the profit screen passes everyone.

breakout.what: A close above the top of a 40- or 60-session base 28% wide or less that was 20% or tighter or tightened before the break, on 1.6 times the usual volume, in the top 45% of the day's range, within the last five sessions and still above it; above the 200-day average with the 50-day at least 98% of it; leader score 45 or more; its industry in the top 60% on money flow and its industry's index within 3% of its 60-session high; a month better than the Nifty 500's; not more than 16% above its 50-day average or 55% up in three months; no known fall in profit over 10% or results sold by the market. Held 63 sessions, left on a close 12% under.
breakout.replay: The site's own engine run on every fifth session; its top fifteen bought at the next open.
breakout.bias: Industries are NSE's list as it stands today, so a company since delisted has no industry here and passes that screen unread. Quarterly results start in 2018 and cover companies listed today; without one a stock is never refused for it.

technical.what: A rising 200-day average with price and the 50-day above it, leader score 55 or more; a low within 1.5% of the 20-day average in the last three sessions and a green close above it, no more than 6% over it; RSI 48 to 68; its industry in the top half on money flow; no known fall in profit over 10%. Held 63 sessions, left on a close 12% under.
technical.replay: The site's own engine run on every fifth session; its top fifteen bought at the next open.
technical.bias: Industries are NSE's list as it stands today, so a company since delisted has no industry here and passes that screen unread. Quarterly results start in 2018 and cover companies listed today; without one a stock is never refused for it.

quick.what: In an uptrend, leader score in the top 35%, a two-day RSI under 10 or a 4% fall in five sessions, still within 3% of its 50-day average, results not just sold. Held 21 sessions, left on a close 10% under.
quick.replay: The site's own engine run on every fifth session; its top fifteen bought at the next open.

flow.what: The three sectors ranked highest on rotation (45% their median stock's three months, 35% the share of their stocks above the 50-day average, 20% their share of turnover this week against sixty sessions); in each, the five strongest stocks in an uptrend, outside the most volatile fifth, within 15% of their high, and ahead of the Nifty 500 over one month and three. Held 63 sessions, left on a close 15% under.
flow.replay: The site's own engine run on every fifth session; its top fifteen bought at the next open.
flow.bias: Sectors are NSE's list as it stands today, so a company since delisted has no sector here and could not be picked.

emerging.what: Companies listed six to eighteen months, above a rising 50-day average, within 10% of their high, leader score 60 or more, ahead of the Nifty 500 over one month and three, no more than 18% over the 50-day, no loss or fall in sales last quarter where one is on file. Held 90 sessions; after 15, left on a close under the 50-day average; at any time on a close 15% under.
emerging.replay: The site's own engine run on every fifth session; its top fifteen bought at the next open.
emerging.bias: Industries are NSE's list as it stands today, so a company since delisted has no industry here and passes that screen unread. Quarterly results start in 2018 and cover companies listed today; without one a stock is never refused for it.

week.note: Replaced by Swing / This month in December 2026; kept as measured, a list every five sessions from 2017 held 5 sessions with a close 7% under as the exit.

young.what: Companies listed six to twelve months, their 6-month return standing in for the 12-month one, placed against the established universe.

momentum.note: Replaced by Long-term compounders in December 2026; kept as measured, a list every five sessions from 2017 held 63 sessions with a close 15% under as the exit.

young.what: Companies listed six to twelve months, their 6-month return standing in for the 12-month one, placed against the established universe.

before.what: The 150 highest technical scores on the exchange, momentum and accumulation setups, Rs 2 crore a day, ordered by the old trade score. Its targets cannot be replayed from prices, so it is shown WITHOUT them, which flatters it.

overlap.what: Names two of the three lists share on the same list date, out of 15: mean_shared over the dates both made a list, dates_with_any_pct the share of those dates with one or more in common. No list gives way to another.

first_version.what: The lists as first built: this month was three parts leader score and one part five-day dip, and momentum did not give way to long term. Same dates, same rules.
